summary: Nîmes runs its city-centre parking through long concessions: Indigo, Q-Park and Interparking operate the car parks, with terms of 11 to 61 years according to local press in January 2026, and the public company SPL Agate runs the on-street spaces under a concession from 2017 to 2027. SPL Agate's activity report for 2023 records that the paid on-street area was extended on 2 October 2023, bringing the city-centre total to 4,829 contracted spaces, with a flat 25-euro post-parking charge. A December 2024 press article set out on-street rules due from 1 January 2025: payment Monday to Friday 9:00-12:00 and 14:00-19:00 and Saturday morning, an 8-hour maximum stay and no reduced post-parking charge. Local press in January 2026, summarising the city's 2024 report, put average weekday car park occupancy at 68% (64% in 2023); it named Arènes and Maison Carrée the most attractive car parks by revenue and visits, and Gare-Feuchères as in decline, but gave no per-car-park occupancy. In October 2024 the city set out a low-emission zone for the whole commune, due from 1 January 2025 under a legal obligation and restricting only unclassified vehicles at first, and opened a public consultation; this check did not confirm that it started or what its current status is. After the 2026 municipal election the new mayor, Vincent Bouget, suspended a planned 318-space car park near the h2 congress centre, a project of the previous administration, pending a new proposal worked out with residents and the delegate Tissot (reported 14 April 2026). A Nîmes Métropole decision transmitted on 10 April 2026 asks the State's Fonds Vert for 80,000 euros towards a 100,000-euro pre-operational phase for a multimodal interchange hub at Caveirac, linked to the planned T5 bus line.

items.text: In the SPL Agate activity report for 2023 (the report is undated; read on 21 October 2026), the on-street tariff table from 2 October 2023 gives 1 euro for 40 minutes and 1.50 euros for an hour in the red zone, and 1 euro for an hour, 2 euros for two hours and 4.50 euros for seven hours in the green zone. The first 30 minutes are free once a day per vehicle and per tariff zone. The post-parking charge (FPS) is a flat 25 euros, which is also the amount shown for the 8-hour maximum stay.
items.source_title: SPL AGATE, compte rendu d'activité 2023 - stationnement payant de voirie, Nîmes

items.text: The city-centre on-street concession run by SPL Agate (2017 to 2027) grew to 4,829 contracted spaces on 2 October 2023, 639 more after the Nord-Gambetta extension, with 283 pay machines. Average daily takings per space fell to 1.76 euros in 2023 from 2.03 euros in 2019.
items.source_title: SPL AGATE, compte rendu d'activité 2023 - stationnement payant de voirie, Nîmes

items.text: Inspectors made 458,931 checks in 2023 and issued 51,215 post-parking charges, 11.16% of checks. The report says vehicle-mounted plate-reading control would start in 2024 to raise spontaneous payment.
items.source_title: SPL AGATE, compte rendu d'activité 2023 - stationnement payant de voirie, Nîmes

items.text: A press article of 21 December 2024 sets out on-street rules due to apply from 1 January 2025: payment Monday to Friday 9:00-12:00 and 14:00-19:00 and Saturday 9:00-12:00, an 8-hour maximum stay, and a flat 25-euro post-parking charge with no reduced rate. It also says that, when the low-emission zone starts on 1 January 2025, residents of Nîmes and Nîmes Métropole with Crit'Air 0 (electric, hydrogen) or Crit'Air 1 (gas, hybrid) vehicles would get two free hours once a day per vehicle in the red and green zones.
items.source_title: NÎMES Quelques modifications dans la gestion du stationnement (Objectif Gard, 21 Dec 2024)

items.text: A city press release of 28 October 2024 said Nîmes had a legal obligation to set up a low-emission zone (ZFE-m) for five years from 1 January 2025, and opened a public consultation on it. It covers the whole commune, and on 1 January 2025 only unclassified vehicles (under 3% of the running car fleet and 12% of heavy trucks) were to be restricted. Motorways (A9, A54), the N106 and N113 and some other routes are exempt routes, and exemptions are possible for vehicles of general interest, public transport and low-mileage drivers (under 8,000 km a year).
items.source_title: Mise en place d'une Zone à faibles émissions (ZFE) : la Ville invite les Nîmois à s'exprimer (press release, 28 Oct 2024)

items.text: In February 2024 the city planned to close five streets around Porte de France, next to the Arènes, to motor traffic with three retractable bollards, removing 20 surface spaces at a cost of 250,000 euros. It expected the large Arènes car park to absorb the displaced parking, and a new circulation plan was due by autumn 2025.
items.source_title: NÎMES Le secteur Porte de France s'aménage doucement mais sûrement (Objectif Gard, 22 Feb 2024)

items.text: In a decision filed on 10 April 2026, the Nîmes Métropole president asked the State's Fonds Vert for 80,000 euros towards a 100,000-euro pre-operational phase (studies, land purchase) for a multimodal hub at Caveirac. The hub is described as linked to the planned T5 high-service bus line between the Vaunage and Nîmes.
items.source_title: Décision FIN2026-03-085, Nîmes Métropole (pôle d'échange multimodal de Caveirac)

items.text: A February 2022 press report on a site visit by the Nîmes Métropole president said the second section of the T2 high-service bus line would enter service in early September 2022, linking the station to the Paloma venue in 15 minutes. It gave 123 million euros, 21 stations and 11.5 km for the whole T2 line. A 400-space park-and-ride at Paloma, shared with the concert hall, was to be available to users.
items.source_title: NÎMES Où en est-on du chantier de la ligne T2 du tram'bus ? (Objectif Gard, 12 Feb 2022)

items.text: On 14 April 2026 the new mayor, Vincent Bouget, suspended a planned 318-space, four-level car park near the h2 congress centre (Placette) after resident opposition. The city will rework it with the delegate Tissot.
items.source_title: NÎMES Parking de la Placette : Vincent Bouget suspend le projet (Objectif Gard, 14 Apr 2026)

items.text: In February 2026 the developers Tissot and GGL, who own parcel EX566 in the city centre, presented a revised project with 318 parking spaces, replacing the programme of a building-permit application filed on 25 October 2022 (63 flats and 219 spaces). They announced a night subscription at 30 euros a month for residents, fast EV chargers and 20 accessible spaces. The new permit was still under review.
items.source_title: NÎMES La Holding Tissot et GGL présentent le projet "Allégorie" (Objectif Gard, 3 Feb 2026)

items.text: Indigo's Porte Auguste car park opened a 16-space secure bike park in early 2025, replacing three car spaces. It costs 4 euros a month or 32 euros a year, and about 16,000 of the roughly 40,000-euro cost was subsidised.
items.source_title: NÎMES Un nouveau cyclopark sécurisé pour les cyclistes Porte Auguste (Objectif Gard, 24 May 2025)

items.text: Car parks are run by Indigo, Q-Park and Interparking, and on-street parking by the public company SPL Agate, under concessions of roughly 11 to 61 years. Indigo's Arènes car park was conceded in 1968 for 61 years, and Interparking holds Les Halles until 2029.
items.source_title: FAIT DU SOIR Stationnement à Nîmes : ce que révèle le rapport sur les parkings payants (Objectif Gard, 6 Jan 2026)

items.text: According to the city's 2024 report, operators paid the city 648,550 euros in fees in 2024, up 25% on 2023, and Arènes and Maison Carrée took 3.3 and 2.4 million euros in revenue. Gare-Feuchères revenue was still 15% below 2019 and its visits had nearly halved since 2019.
items.source_title: FAIT DU SOIR Stationnement à Nîmes : ce que révèle le rapport sur les parkings payants (Objectif Gard, 6 Jan 2026)

items.text: The city's 2024 report puts average weekday occupancy (9:00-18:00) at 68%, up from 64% in 2023, with about 800 free spaces even at peak and 3,616 subscribers. Arènes and Maison Carrée peak between 10:00 and 16:00, especially on Fridays, and 26% of tickets are free (48% at Arènes).
items.source_title: FAIT DU SOIR Stationnement à Nîmes : ce que révèle le rapport sur les parkings payants (Objectif Gard, 6 Jan 2026)

items.text: The City of Nîmes' 2021 annual report for the Maison Carrée car park (undated; read on 21 October 2026) names Sopark as the contract holder and Indigo Park as the operator. The 545-space car park runs under a concession signed on 21 April 1986 that ends on 12 August 2036. Hourly visits, paid and free, were 268,859 in 2021 against 333,466 in 2019, and the report lists one EV charging point.
items.source_title: Sopark/Indigo, Parc Maison Carrée, rapport d'activité 2021 (Ville de Nîmes)

items.text: Q-Park runs the 466-space Jean Jaurès car park and 1,232 on-street spaces under a 2006 contract with a 45-year term. The car park had 62,832 hourly entries in 2023, 4% fewer than in 2022, and charged 4.00 euros for two hours. The report is undated (read on 21 October 2026).
items.source_title: Q-Park, Nîmes Parking Jean Jaurès & voirie, rapport d'activité 2023

items.text: The Q-Park activity report for 2023 on the Jean Jaurès contract (undated; read on 21 October 2026) lists 82,000 euros of investment in 2023: 18 pay machines for the on-street extension, 10 EV charging points (bornes IRVE) and repainting of operating premises. The car park's data sheet lists 10 EV spaces alongside a capacity of 466.
items.source_title: Q-Park, Nîmes Parking Jean Jaurès & voirie, rapport d'activité 2023

gaps: Ville de Nîmes 'Observatoire parkings 2021' and 'Observatoire voirie 2021' PDFs (nimes.fr/fileadmin/mediatheque_commune/Publications_actes_administratifs/rapports_delegataires/2021/Observatoire_parkings_2021.pdf and Observatoire_voirie_2021.pdf) returned 404, so no per-car-park capacity or utilisation table from the city was read.

The 2024 municipal parking report itself was not found; the 2024 figures come only from the Objectif Gard summary (https://www.objectifgard.com/gard/nimes/fait-du-soir-stationnement-a-nimes-ce-que-revele-le-rapport-sur-les-parkings-payants-157549.php). Arènes car park capacity, tariffs and any works were not confirmed from an official page.

Roole Media article on parking prices and EV chargers before the 2026 municipal election (https://media.roole.fr/transition/territoires/nimes-stationnement-trop-cher-manque-de-bornes-de-recharge-la-mobilite-au-cour-des-debats-avant-les-municipales) showed only its table of contents, not the body text, so it was not used.

Nîmes Métropole T1 southern extension press kit (https://www.nimes-metropole.fr/fileadmin/mediatheque/Dossier-commun/Documentations/Dossiers_de_presse/DP_INAUG_T1_Sud-BD.pdf) and T2 inauguration press kit (DP-T2-Inauguration-Janvier-2020.pdf) returned 404 or could not be read; the T1/T2 park-and-ride capacities at opening were not confirmed. Only the planned 400-space Paloma park-and-ride (Feb 2022 press) was read.
No Nîmes open-data feed for car park availability was found, and no official count of public EV chargers or any Nîmes Métropole parking data portal was located.
Current status of the Nîmes ZFE in 2026 (after the 2026 national debate on abolishing ZFEs) was not verified from an official or readable source; the ZFE items describe the October 2024 plan only.
The text of the Écusson pedestrian-area order (CIR-AP-2019-00095) and any Écusson or Arènes traffic plan for 2025-2026 was not found or read; the Porte de France item is the February 2024 plan only.

No 2025 or 2026 on-street tariff decision by the new municipality (elected March 2026) and no SPL Agate or Q-Park/Indigo 2024 annual reports were found. The WebSearch budget ran out before Midi Libre, ICI Gard Lozère, Indigo/Q-Park web pages and the Nîmes Métropole parc-relais pages could be searched.
